findings.note: Voted nay on ending debate on an amendment requiring voters to show photo identification. Cloture failed, 53 yeas to 47 nays, 3/5 needed.

findings.note: Voted nay on a procedural motion tied to the House message carrying the SAVE America Act (proof of citizenship to register, photo ID to vote).

findings.motion: Roll call 57, motion to proceed to the House message to accompany S. 1383 (SAVE America Act vehicle); agreed to 51-48
findings.note: Voted nay on the motion to begin Senate consideration of the House message carrying the SAVE America Act.

findings.passage: This is a fraud masquerading as an election integrity effort.
findings.note: Caption on his official video page about the SAVE America Act, which the page describes as a bill designed to make it harder for certain citizens to vote. Issued in his name.

findings.passage: In Congress, Senator Van Hollen is fighting to pass the Freedom to Vote Act, legislation he has cosponsored that would establish a minimum set of national standards to ensure that our fellow citizens can make their voices heard at the ballot box.
findings.note: Issue page on his official site (undated) says he cosponsored the Freedom to Vote Act, a national minimum-standards voting bill. The page does not mention voter ID by name.

findings.passage: “Nobody is going to risk going to prison for six years in order to cast a vote in an election,” Van Hollen said. “I mean that defies common sense and it also defies the facts, which is why Republicans can’t come up with any proof.”
findings.note: Quoted by WBAL Baltimore News from his Senate floor remarks on the SAVE America Act. He says there is no evidence of widespread non-citizen voting. WBAL also reports that he said the bill will disenfranchise millions of voters (reporter's words, not his).

findings.passage: Today, in a sickening display of political cowardice, an undemocratic minority of senators blocked a series of bills that would help reduce gun violence, including a bipartisan compromise proposal to close gaping loopholes in current law and keep guns out of the hands of criminals and people with severe mental illnesses – a proposal that has the support of 90 percent of Americans.
findings.note: His statement as a House member, printed in full by Bethesda Magazine, after the Senate blocked the 2013 background-check compromise. Date is the article date.

findings.passage: We have a long tradition in this country of responsible gun ownership – but in the wake of too many tragedies, including the massacre in Newtown, we are clearly not doing enough to keep our citizens safe.
findings.note: Same 2013 statement. Mentions responsible gun ownership and says current action is not enough.

findings.passage: The Supreme Court's decision to interfere with common-sense concealed carry laws will ultimately result in more guns on our streets and less safe communities.
findings.note: Joint statement issued in the names of both Maryland senators and six House members (he is one), after the Bruen ruling and Maryland's suspension of its 'good and substantial reason' carry-permit standard. Posted on Rep. Raskin's site; month taken from the URL.

findings.passage: Now more than ever, we are committed to pushing for federal gun safety reforms that are proven to better protect our communities and are overwhelmingly supported by the American people.
findings.note: Same joint statement; commits the signers to federal gun safety reforms.
